in_hebrew.name: קוללי
in_hebrew.long_meaning: קוללי הוא שם שמקורו אולי בקול, קולו של האל או קולו של ישוע. שם זה עשוי להיות קשור לנושא של שמיעה וקשב, שכן הקול הוא אמצעי חשוב לתקשורת עם האל ועם בני אדם אחרים. במשמעות רחבה יותר, קוללי עשוי לסמל את הנאמנות והמסירות לישוע ולדבריו.

in_greek.name: Κόλλυ
in_greek.long_meaning: Κόλλυ είναι ένα όνομα που πιθανόν να συνδέεται με την έννοια της προσκόλλησης ή της αφοσίωσης. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, η προσκόλληση στον Θεό ή στον Ιησού είναι ένα επαναλαμβανόμενο θέμα. Το όνομα Κόλλυ μπορεί να συμβολίζει την πιστότητα και την αφοσίωση στον Θεό και στη διδασκαλία του Ιησού.

data.cultural_impact: The name Collie does not have a direct historical or cultural impact on Christianity. However, it is interesting to note that in medieval Europe, dogs were often used symbolically in religious art and literature. For example, St. Christopher, the patron saint of travelers, is sometimes depicted with a dog by his side, representing faithfulness and protection. In this sense, the name Collie, with its association with dogs, may symbolize steadfastness or loyal protection in one's Christian faith.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Collie can be seen as a reminder of the faithful and unwavering love of God for His people. Just as a collie dog is known for its loyalty and devotion to its owner, so too does God remain steadfast in His love for us. Additionally, the name may be seen as a reflection of the idea that we, as Christians, are called to be faithful and devoted servants of God, emulating the loyal and unwavering nature of a collie dog. Ultimately, the name Collie offers a unique and meaningful connection to the broader themes of faithfulness, steadfastness, and devotion within the Christian faith.

This name has been used in various Scottish communities and has been adopted by some Christian families due to its strong association with faith and loyalty. Despite its Scottish roots, the name Collie has gained popularity beyond Scotland and is now recognized and cherished in various Christian communities worldwide.
